reviewer_role: Author; personally read all complete actual source units, chosen targets, necessary context, and all complete source-target-category-rationale triples separately before freeze.
review_method: Read all 133 complete actual source units in chapters 10–14 (14/47/41/14/17), complete proposed targets and surrounding narrative context. Separately reread every complete source/target/category/rationale triple in unclipped batches 1–25, 26–50, 51–75, 76–100, and 101–133 through complete_text. Preserved the immutable original author draft. Five complete row refinements retain undefined ariels, explicit Baithlaem/Bethlehem wording, distinct roster wording and divine commands, and replace the geddour campaign comparison with its immediate Manassite grammatical antecedent; all five changed complete triples were separately reread after editing. Meaningful local roster headings are explicitly labelled same-chapter and state the named line’s actual grammatical role or assembly purpose. This is an initial supplied-English curated pass, not exhaustive discovery, independent specialist approval, original-language analysis, apparatus review, numerical reconciliation, or identification of differently named people.
pin_method: Freshly fetched exact raw files at the immutable commit for all five used books, verified full Git blob SHA1 against the source-check registry covering the thirteen existing source books, saved separate raw author-current files and SHA256 receipts, and verified full parsed equality with the actual local source cache. Rehashed all saved raw files and rechecked parsed equality at author freeze. No new book metadata lookup was required; all five used books were already in those fixed source-check registries.

old_row.relationship: Warrior-deed parallel: Moabite opponents and a lion in snow
old_row.rationale: Both accounts describe the warrior’s deeds against two Moabite opponents and a lion in a pit or cistern on a snowy day. Chronicles says two ariels; Samuel says two sons of Ariel, preserving the distinct objects.

new_row.relationship: Warrior-deed parallel: striking in Moab and a lion in snow
new_row.rationale: Both accounts describe striking two in Moab and a lion in a pit or cistern on a snowy day. Chronicles says two ariels; Samuel says two sons of Ariel, preserving the distinct objects without defining Chronicles’ ariels.

old_row.relationship: Warrior-list parallel: Joab’s brother and a Bethlehem warrior
old_row.rationale: Both roster openings name Joab’s brother and a second warrior linked to Dodo or Dodi and Bethlehem, while retaining their different personal name forms and Samuel’s explicit membership among the thirty.

new_row.relationship: Warrior-list parallel: Joab’s brother and a Bethlehem warrior
new_row.rationale: Both roster openings name Joab’s brother and a second warrior linked to Dodo and Baithlaem in Chronicles or Dodi and Bethlehem in Samuel, retaining their different personal and place name forms and Samuel’s explicit membership among the thirty.

old_row.relationship: Warrior-roster parallel: the Tekoite family description and Abiezer
old_row.rationale: Both roster passages include a Tekoite described through an Ekkes or Ikkesh father-name and Abiezer the Anathothite. The link retains the two rosters’ wording rather than resolving their variant name forms.

new_row.relationship: Warrior-roster parallel: the Tekoite family description and Abiezer
new_row.rationale: Both roster passages include a Tekoite described through an Ekkes or Ikkesh father-name and Abiezer the Anathothite. The link compares those stated descriptions while preserving each roster’s distinct personal and family wording.

old_row.relationship: Narrative campaign connection with bounded identification: David and the geddour
old_row.rationale: Chronicles says the newly listed men fought alongside David against the Geddour; Samuel describes David inquiring about pursuit of a geddour and setting out with his men. Samuel does not name these Manassite leaders, so their individual participation is not supplied from that passage.

new_row.relationship: Same-chapter grammatical connection: the Manassite leaders fight beside David
new_row.rationale: The pronoun they follows the seven named leaders of Manasseh’s thousands who joined David on the way to Soklag. This identifies the source’s unnamed fighting companions through the immediate roster and connects their recorded leadership with their aid in battle.

old_row.relationship: Historical speech parallel with distinct approach wording: a changed tactic
old_row.rationale: Both record David asking God again and receiving instructions to turn away rather than make the earlier approach. Chronicles directs approach near pear trees; Samuel speaks of the place of weeping, preserving the distinct directions and site wording.

new_row.relationship: Historical speech parallel with distinct approach wording: a changed tactic
new_row.rationale: Both record David asking God again and receiving instructions to turn away and approach elsewhere. Chronicles says not to go behind them and to approach near pear trees; Samuel says not to go up to meet them and names the place of weeping, preserving the distinct commands.

editorial_notes: Chapter 12 contains 41 actual source units in this edition; none were renumbered to a familiar forty-verse arrangement.
Saul’s whole-house death notice, Samuel’s armour-bearer notice, distinct trophy locations, sons, and burial objects are preserved.

The warrior comparisons preserve three hundred wounded versus eight hundred slain, sword versus spear, barley versus lentils, differently introduced actors, thirty versus three, and distinct royal appointments. No independent name-equivalence or identity equation is claimed.

Bare names in the continuing warrior and helper rosters are connected to explicit same-chapter grammatical headings or summaries; no deed, clan identity, or ancestry absent from the source is invented.
Ark route wording, the explicit hand-on-ark cause, calf movement, different instruments, and each householder’s source form remain distinct.

David’s order to burn abandoned gods is related to Deuteronomy’s command without claiming the execution of the order was narrated. Pear-tree and place-of-weeping instructions retain each passage’s actual wording.

before.relationship: Narrative setting: David receives a country town while away from Saul
before.rationale: Chronicles introduces helpers joining David at Soklag while he was kept from Saul; Samuel narrates Achish granting David the country town Ziklag. Each passage’s place form is retained.

after.relationship: Narrative setting: David’s separation from Saul
after.rationale: Chronicles places the helpers’ arrival during David’s separation from Saul. Samuel narrates David deciding to escape Saul, moving with his men into the foreigners’ land, and Saul ceasing pursuit; it supplies the earlier setting without identifying the later helpers individually.

changes.reason: Target alone omitted Saul and could depend on unresolved Soklag/Ziklag identification. Replacement targets the explicit David–Saul narrative setting and avoids that equation.
